fieldValues.title: Essay image formats and size
fieldValues.decision_question: Which image formats may an image paragraph hold, and how large may each file be?
fieldValues.context: The web editor's attachment defaults are 1 MB per file and text only (srs-web#693). The owner, 2026-11-04 (vignette a5fa4798): 'We still want to generally limit those files. This is not a place for big files.' The owner, 2026-11-08 (vignette 02e02668): 'Lets support svgs without scripts.' A repository's attachment_policy can narrow or widen limits (I-107).
fieldValues.friction: With text-only defaults no image can be attached at all; with no limit, repositories swell past the browser budget (vignette 47326128).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. PNG, JPEG, WebP and script-free SVG, at most 1 MB each (recommended). For: covers photos, screenshots and diagrams; keeps the existing per-file cap. Against: a large photo must be resized first.
B. The same plus GIF. For: simple animation. Against: large files, little need in essays.
C. A larger cap, such as 5 MB. For: no resizing. Against: against 'not a place for big files'.
D. Leave text only. Against: the feature cannot work.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Small files; formats every browser shows; SVG only without scripts (owner).
fieldValues.decision_statement: An essay image is a PNG, JPEG, WebP or script-free SVG file of at most 1 MB, unless the repository's attachment policy sets a stricter limit.
fieldValues.rationale: These four formats cover photos, screenshots and diagrams in every browser, and the existing 1 MB cap keeps attachments small as the owner asked.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers often hit the cap with ordinary images, or ask for a format outside the list.
